extracted.intended_audience: directors, stage managers, performers, costume/set designers and opera companies staging this libretto/scene
extracted.subtask_description: Staging and performing a scene from a 19th‑century grand opera/libretto, including chorus movement, musical cues, character blocking, costumes, and set changes. The page provides scripted dialogue plus explicit stage directions and scenic/costume detail to realize the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chorus composition and simultaneous entrance
rubrics_metrics.description: The CHORUS enters. (It consists of two semi-choruses which enter at the same time from opposite sides...)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each semi-chorus should enter simultaneously from opposite sides, march round the stage, and range themselves in rows on the side by which they entered. One semi-chorus is composed of young knights, the other of older ones; each semi-chorus must have a distinct costume and ensigns. When the two choruses stand opposite each other, the march ceases and the two leaders speak. (Text even lists named members and follower counts for each semi-chorus.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use musical cues for entrances/exits and dramatic signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical signals (e.g., trumpets; music heard from an opposite direction that becomes gradually louder) mark arrivals, departures, and shifts in attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ trumpet blasts and offstage music to herald approaching characters ('the trumpet's blast, that tells in warlike accents My sons are near') and to accompany exits/entrances ('Exit DIEGO. Music is heard in an opposite direction, and becomes gradually louder'). Coordinate sound crescendos with onstage revealing and movement for dramatic emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocking and physical gestures tied to emotional beats
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed stage directions prescribe steps, embraces, receding, pauses and other movements connected to emotion (e.g., 'She recedes one or two steps', 'They rush into each other's arms').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should follow micro-blocking described to convey internal states: use receding steps to give space, suppressed emotion with pauses and withheld demonstrations, sudden embraces to signify reconciliation, and startled gestures (e.g., Beatrice 'starting back in horror'). Timing of these gestures relative to lines is part of the dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set architecture for reveals (folding-doors and scene changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The folding-doors at the back of the stage are thrown open. Scene changes to distinct locales are specified (e.g., 'The scene changes to a garden opening on the sea.' 'The scene changes to a chamber in the interior of the palace.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stage architecture (folding doors, alcoves) and clear scenic transitions to frame revelations and entrances. Arrange scenic elements (garden opening to sea, alcove, palace chamber) so entrances/exits and visual reveals read clearly to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costume/visual differentiation of groups and characters
rubrics_metrics.description: One semi-chorus consists of young knights, the other of older ones, each has its peculiar costume and ensigns. Detailed costume and prop suggestions for the bride and procession appear in-speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate choruses and character cohorts by costume and insignia (age, rank). For the bride and ceremonial moments, follow the libretto's rich costume notes (sandals, snow‑white tissue, purple-and-gold girdle, silk mantle, diadem of gems, veil to the feet, myrtle wreath, pearls and coral, palfrey with purple housings and gem-bright bridle). These visual specifics support character status and pageant spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leader-solo speaking roles within choral structure
rubrics_metrics.description: When the two choruses stand opposite to each other, the march ceases, and the two leaders speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate chorus leaders who can break into spoken (or solo) delivery while the chorus frames the scene. Ensure the transition from choral music/marching to leader speech is clean (march stops, leaders step forward) and that leaders' lines are projected/acted distinct from mass chorus passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional vocal direction and tempo of delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages direct actors to convey specific inward states (e.g., 'with suppressed emotion', 'after awaiting for some time', 'with manifest absence of mind').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should modulate tempo, dynamic and timbre to match stage directions: suppressed voice for inward grief, pauses for withheld feeling, abstracted mien for trance-like joy. Pace recitatives and arioso lines to allow emotional beats and reactions to register before the next action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-specific blocking for private encounters amid public spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: Private encounters (Don Manuel describing secret bride; Beatrice's solo anguish; Don Caesar leading Beatrice before the chorus) occur within a public, ceremonial context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage private emotional moments (intimate aside, secret rendezvous) in contrast to the public procession: use alcoves, sequestered garden paths, or pulled-back chorus to create intimacy. The chorus may be asked to 'step aside' or 'withdraw to the background' to frame a private scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pauses and dramatic silence to heighten revelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Several directions call for waiting and pauses ('after awaiting for some time', 'after a pause', 'She listens', 'He pauses'), especially before revelations and reconciliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement silences and measured waits before key revelations (mother revealing the sister; brothers' reconciliation) so audience tension and the emotional impact of the disclosure are heightened. Coordinate with lighting and musical rests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic and prop details to support character intentions and pageantry
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed image-making lines specify props and scenic elements (bazaar with fabrics, palfrey to carry the bride, trumpets, jewelled diadems, bracelets, bracelets, veil).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realize these descriptive elements in set dressing and props: bazaar stalls for costume selection, appropriate horses or palfrey (or symbolic substitute), and parade accoutrements for processions. These tangible details underpin the prince's intentions and create the ceremonial atmosphere described in the libretto.
